newsitem.title: FRANCE: French minister puts questionmark on Juppe.
newsitem.headline: French minister puts questionmark on Juppe.

text.p: Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre put a question mark on the future of Prime Minister Alain Juppe on Monday with an ambiguous statement about who would hold the job after France's general election.

"Taking into account what we have heard during the campaign, we will need a new team, a new prime minister and it will be up to the President (Jacques Chirac) to choose that new prime minister," Debre told France-2 television during a campaign tour of western France.
In French, Debre's words could equally refer to Juppe being replaced by another politician or simply mean Juppe could be appointed anew for the post.
"Alain Juppe's own friends are today asking questions about his future but this could all just be part of an election tactic," France-2 commented.
Juppe is leader of the campaign by the ruling centre-right coalition to keep a majority in parliament in the May 25-June 1 election.
But the prime minister and aides have clearly realised his record unpopularity was playing against the coalition and have coyly hinted in recent days he was not assured of keeping the post.
Juppe said on Sunday he was not campaigning to keep the job.
"I'm absolutely not a candidate for my own succession," Juppe then told TF1 television. "It would be very arrogant and insolent to say 'it's me'. It's absurd. It is the president who decides."

Opinion polls in late 1996 showed that Juppe, 51, was the least popular prime minister in the Fifth Republic, blamed for record unemployment and austerity to help France qualify for a single European currency. The Socialist and Communist opposition has made him their central target.
"My only ambition is to help to win this campaign because I believe it is in the interest of France" for the centre-right coalition to keep its National Assembly majority, he said.
But Juppe did not say he would refuse the post if offered to him again and specialists say he was still the logical choice.
